source_review.notes: Checked current official UEFI 2.11 and ACPI 6.6 specification access, Devicetree 0.4, the RISC-V SBI repository, Trusted Firmware-A design, and Linux AArch64/EFI boot guidance. Six endpoints returned HTTP 200; UEFI pages were accessible through the browser but rejected the command-line probe with HTTP 403, which is recorded as access behavior rather than content failure.

evidence: Checked stage/handoff, half-open range, ownership, authorization, measurement, map-generation, service-lifecycle, and machine-description notation.
Checked hexadecimal bases, KiB sizes, endpoints, privilege and lifecycle states.
notation_and_syntax.notes: All range calculations require checked arithmetic in the implemented address width.

evidence: Recomputed a 96 KiB kernel end at 0x80218000 and a 32 KiB Devicetree end at 0x80220000.
Recomputed no kernel/Devicetree overlap and a 4 KiB Devicetree/reserved overlap.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduces every expected endpoint and overlap result.

evidence: Re-derived half-open overlap as max(0,min(end)-max(base)) after checked end computation.
Reviewed handoff_ok as authorization, bounds, ownership, visibility, ABI, and lifecycle conjunction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Adjacent half-open ranges are disjoint; endpoint arithmetic must precede comparisons safely.

evidence: Reviewed integer wrap, zero/oversized segments, overlaps, invalid entries, stale map keys, malformed tables, missing extensions, duplicate references, and decompression bombs.
Reviewed power-cut updates, rollback, unsigned recovery, multicore timeout, cache incoherence, post-exit calls, runtime mapping error, and evidence mismatch.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Successful boot is insufficient without negative-path ownership and security evidence.

invariant_checking.notes: Fifteen obligations cover reset through durable recovery.

evidence: Reviewed typed handoff refinement and the single ownership cut from predecessor publication to successor acquisition.
Constructed counterexamples for unchecked end arithmetic, checksum-as-authentication, stale UEFI map keys, post-exit service calls, release without barriers, and verified boot without rollback.
proof_review.notes: Stage-local proofs compose only when security state and reserved resources remain monotonic.

evidence: Audited reset state, authenticated, authorized, measured, verified, rollback-protected, immutable, runtime, reserved, atomic, and fail-closed terminology.
Confirmed invented address values and deterministic range model are labeled.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Verification, measurement, authorization, and rollback are distinct claims.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CA-048/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, Python toolchain, and environment.
Reviewed conformance, parser fuzzing, emulation, physical boot, power-cut, negative secure-boot, multicore, and runtime-service evidence requirements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing snippet establishes deterministic address-range auditing only.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed firmware boot as a graph of typed, authenticated, lifecycle-bound ownership transfers rather than a byte-loading sequence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed reset resources, memory/coherence initialization, defensive loaders, UEFI/ACPI/Devicetree/SBI, ABI/privilege handoff, multicore, runtime services, virtualization, updates, recovery, logs, fuzzing, and evidence. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from reset and image loading through machine descriptions and service lifetimes to secure update/recovery, followed by fifteen obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-six misconceptions, ten examples, and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external firmware/boot architect, UEFI/ACPI/Devicetree/SBI maintainer, silicon/board/kernel/hypervisor engineer, cryptographer, secure-update/attestation specialist, formal-verification reviewer, or platform certification is claimed.
